target_customer: Small to midsize insurers, MGAs and MGUs, captives, risk retention groups and program managers
problem: Small insurers run on spreadsheets and filing cabinets and spend heavily on administration; the YC page claims up to 60 percent of revenue goes to administrative expense.
business_model: B2B SaaS insurance management platform sold to insurers and programs
product_category: Insurance core system and operations software

founders.name: Cameron MacArthur
founders.background_notes: Listed as the only founder on the YC page. One search summary cites a co-founder and a prior DARPA, Adobe and Northwestern background from a profile site, but I could not confirm either in an opened source, so they are not recorded.

competitors.name: Duck Creek Technologies
competitors.what: Core insurance suite (policy, billing, claims) that its filing says can serve smaller carriers
competitors.traction_then: Established vendor; named in the Aite 2019 US property and casualty core systems evaluation
competitors.funding_then: Preparing a public listing in 2019 (draft registration statement)

technical_complexity.rationale: Full insurance operations platform covering policy, billing, claims and filings requires broad product scope and compliance, but is standard enterprise software engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Core systems are sticky once an insurer migrates, and the platform later added HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance, but sales cycles are long and incumbents are strong.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy the small insurer niche in any source found; the company is still operating in 2025 and now targets MGAs and programs.

market_need_then: Insurance carriers have long used legacy systems; the company claims small insurers waste up to 60 percent of revenue on administration. No independent 2019 source for this figure was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and benefit focused (all in one insurance management software)

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive name that is hard to search because many AI and insurance companies use similar words; the same search returned many unrelated AI insurance firms and no brand press.

outcome_analysis: AI Insurance appears to have kept operating since its 2019 batch, selling an all in one platform to insurance programs, with the site claiming over 100 programs and its CEO appearing on an insurtech podcast in September 2025. Funding is unverified, the competitive position against Duck Creek and Guidewire is untested in sources, and the evidence is too thin to attribute success or failure factors.
notes: Funding is only in aggregators: Seedtable lists a $5.0M seed in March 2019 (Y Combinator, MAGIC Fund, Green Visor Capital, Haymaker Ventures) and Foundernest lists $3.8M in March 2022; the Seedtable page returned 403 and the figures conflict, so no round is recorded. The Duck Creek filing is dated 2019, probably several months after the Winter 2019 batch; its exact date was not opened. Guidewire, Majesco and Insurity appear only in undated or later pages, so only Duck Creek is listed. A search summary names a co-founder, Thomas Piccirello, and Mountain View headquarters from MarketScreener; not confirmed. Outcome search found no acquisition, layoffs or shutdown. Founder education not found. The YC page lists San Francisco and New York; the company site says San Francisco. Second search: Marketscreener names Thomas Piccirello as a co-founder and former CTO, but only aggregators say so and no YC or company page confirms it, so he is not added.
